chain.g: cause, lawsuit, legal action, complaint, issue, dispute

ety.text: From Middle English sake (“sake, cause”), from Old English sacu (“cause, lawsuit, legal action, complaint, issue, dispute”), from Proto-West Germanic *saku, from Proto-Germanic *sakō (“affair, thing, charge, accusation, matter”), from Proto-Indo-European *seh₂g- (“to investigate”).

ex: I hope you're right, for all our sakes!
It's not worth risking your life for the sake of getting there a few minutes earlier.

senses.d: The benefit or regard of someone or something.
ex:
2005, Plato, Sophist. Translation by Lesley Brown. 242a-b.
But it will be for your sake that we'll undertake to refute this thesis, […]
Ne ãd except thoſe dayes ſhulde be ſhoꝛtened / ſhulde no fleſſe be faved: Butt foꝛ the choſens ſake thoſe dayes ſhalbe ſhoꝛtened.

senses.d: Contention, strife; guilt, sin, accusation or charge.
